brands.domainNotes: aai.sk is confirmed as the official site of AAI, a Slovak high-end audio manufacturer. It makes high-end audio cables (power, speaker, interconnect, RCA, XLR/AES-EBU, COAX, LAN) across the Estremo, Assoluto+, Maestoso 2+ and Vittorioso+ series, plus acoustic isolation Pads and audio Fuses, all using their proprietary Interference Suppression Technology (IST). Bilingual site (Slovak default at aai.sk, English at aai.sk/en/).
brands.notes: No downloadable documentation (PDF/ZIP manuals, datasheets, brochures, spec sheets, catalogues, guides, or white papers) was found anywhere on aai.sk after deep-crawling ~9 pages including the homepage, products index, product-category pages, an individual product page, the IST technology page, FAQ, and reviews. The site has no Support/Downloads/Resources/Manuals/Archive section. All product specifications (connector types, dimensions, materials) are presented inline as HTML text rather than as downloadable files. The Reviews page links to some external review sites, but those are off-domain and were discarded per instructions. No aai.sk-hosted document files exist to record.

brands.domainNotes: The hint domain aavik-acoustics.com issues a 301 redirect to https://audiogroupdenmark.com/aavik-acoustics/. Audio Group Denmark is the manufacturer that owns the AAVIK brand (alongside Ansuz, Borresen, Axxess); the page self-identifies as the official AAVIK site. All document URLs are on the official audiogroupdenmark.com domain. Confirmed as the correct, genuine manufacturer site.
sectionsChecked: https://audiogroupdenmark.com/wp-json/wp/v2/media?mime_type=application/pdf&search=aavik&per_page=100 (site's own media metadata API, JSON only — no document files were downloaded)
brands.notes: The public downloads hub (/material/) is entirely JavaScript-rendered, so WebFetch could not read the document anchors from the HTML, and the Chrome browser extension was not connected. I therefore enumerated the documents through the site's own WordPress REST media API on the official domain (wp-json/wp/v2/media, mime_type=application/pdf), which returns only file metadata (title + source_url) — I did not fetch or download any PDF. WebFetch's summarizer truncates large JSON responses to ~10-12 items per call, so I queried multiple orderings (date asc/desc, title asc/desc) and unioned the results to assemble the complete manual set below. Documents are AAVIK user manuals/guides in English (ENG/English/GB) and German (ger). I deliberately EXCLUDED press/review/award reprint PDFs that are also hosted on the official domain (e.g. hi-fi+ awards, Fidelity/AVGuide reviews, PRODUKTNEWS) because they are marketing/press clippings, not product documentation. There may be a small number of additional manuals not surfaced due to the API truncation, but all major current and legacy AAVIK product lines are covered. The I-188/288/588 English manual exists as two distinct files (a base '_ENG_web' and an '_ENG-1-1_web' revision) — both are included.

brands.notes: Site confirmed as the official ACCUSTIC ARTS (Audio GmbH) manufacturer site. Two document types found: (1) per-product Brochures ("Broschüre") on each current product page under /produkte/, and (2) User Manuals ("Bedienungsanleitung", all in German) plus one USB driver and a warranty PDF on the central /downloads/ page. The download PDFs/ZIP are all served via the site's own WP Rocket CDN mirror host (4a8cd7c2.delivery.rocketcdn.me) rather than the bare accusticarts.de host — this is the manufacturer's own asset delivery, and URLs are recorded exactly as linked. Filenames are inconsistent (ACCUSTIC-ARTS-*, Accustic-Arts-*, Datenblatt_*, Produktblatt_*), so each product page was fetched individually rather than guessing URLs. Legacy/archive models (AMP II MK4, AMP III MK2, MONO II MK2, MONO III MK2, PLAYER I, PLAYER II, POWER I, TUBE DAC II MK3, TUBE PHONO II, TUBE PREAMP II MK2) only have German user manuals on the downloads page; they are marked legacy=true. Did not fetch any .pdf/.zip file directly per instructions. All 16 current products carry a brochure; total 28 unique documents (16 brochures + 10 manuals + 1 driver + 1 warranty).

brands.domainNotes: audes.ee self-identifies as the manufacturer "Audes - Crafted in Estonia, Respected Worldwide," a loudspeaker and amplifier maker since 1938. Homepage, product categories, and footer all consistently brand as AUDES. This is unambiguously the brand's own official manufacturer site. The hint domain audes.ee was correct.
brands.notes: The official AUDES site (audes.ee) hosts almost no downloadable documentation. Across a thorough crawl of the homepage, all product category pages (Loudspeakers, Reference, Excellence AMT, M Series, Credo, Maestro, Credenza, Universal Line, Custom Series, Electronics, Valve Amplifiers, Power Conditioners, Accessories, Speaker Drivers, Transformers), both archive pages (product-archive-loudspeakers, product-archive-amplifiers), and several individual product pages (ATA-134, Excellence 5 AMT, Excellence 3 AMT), only ONE unique downloadable file was found: the Excellence AMT brochure PDF at https://audes.ee/static/excellence_amt.pdf. This same PDF is linked from both the Excellence 5 AMT and Excellence 3 AMT product pages (deduplicated to a single URL). All other product pages present specifications as inline HTML tables and a visual configurator rather than downloadable manuals/datasheets. The two archive (legacy/discontinued) pages list historical models with inline specs only, no document downloads and no links to individual archived product pages. There is no dedicated Downloads/Support/Manuals section on the site. Per instructions, the PDF itself was NOT fetched/downloaded — only recorded. Language marked EN based on the site's default English pages; an Estonian (/et/) mirror of the site exists but was not found to host any distinct additional documents.

METHOD: The /material/ download hub renders links via JavaScript dropdowns (href=javascript:void(0)), so neither WebFetch nor the product pages expose direct file URLs. LEGACY/GAPS: The Z-series (Z1/Z2/Z3/Z5) and 0-series (05/03/01/02) - older generations - have NO dedicated user-guide PDFs in the library; only a Z3 brochure and press reviews exist. The newest A-series and M8 Gold Signature have no docs uploaded yet.

brands.domainNotes: The hint domain cayin.com resolves and is Cayin-branded, but it self-identifies as "Cayin Audio Distribution GmbH — High-End Hifi Online Shop," i.e. Cayin's official European distribution arm / shop rather than the manufacturer's corporate HQ site. It is not an independent third-party reseller; it operates under the Cayin name and hosts official Cayin PDF manuals and catalogues on its own domain (cayin.com/ca-inhalte/uploads/...). I attempted to confirm and prefer the manufacturer's own primary sites, but all were unreachable: en.cayin.cn 302-redirects to an Aliyun "manual_stop" hosting-suspended page; cayinaudio.com and cayin.com.cn / www.cayin.com.cn repeatedly returned "Socket is closed" (down/unreachable). Because the only functioning official Cayin-operated site is the distribution GmbH shop (a distributor in the strict legal sense), I flag confidence as uncertain. All URLs recorded below are strictly on the official cayin.com domain; third-party firmware links (Google Drive, referenced for N8ii and iDAP-8 firmware) were discarded per the rules. Documents are a mix of confirmed direct PDF URLs and, where not drilled into due to fetch budget, the official-domain landing pages that host each document.
brands.notes:
IMPORTANT DOMAIN CAVEAT: cayin.com is Cayin's official European distribution arm ("Cayin Audio Distribution GmbH"), not the manufacturer's HQ site. Hence domainConfidence=uncertain. If strict manufacturer-only sourcing is required, none of these could be confirmed live.

LANGUAGE: Most manuals are German (DE) as this is the German distribution site; several ship bilingual (CP6, HA-300A MK2, Soul 170C provide separate EN PDFs; catalogues are DE/EN). No dedicated Legacy/Discontinued/Archive section exists on this site, so no legacy=true items were marked.

brands.notes:
Identity confirmed: davis-acoustics.com is the official Davis Acoustics (France) site. Documentation is spread across three places: (1) global catalogues + user manual linked in the footer/archives, (2) per-model 'fiche technique' datasheets on each product page (each labelled 'Telechargez la fiche technique en PDF'), and (3) DIY kit spec sheets on /kits/. Every URL is on the official domain; per the task rules I recorded URLs only and did NOT fetch any PDF/JPG files.

Coverage note: Davis Acoustics has ~40 individual loudspeaker product pages (Stellar, Heritage: The Wall/The Stage/The Pledge; Capsule; Courbet S2; Courbet; Krypton; Ariane; D-Max; In-Wall series). Within the WebFetch budget I sampled 9 representative product pages and confirmed most carry a single per-model 'fiche technique' PDF following predictable /wp-content/uploads/ paths. The remaining product pages (e.g. The Stage, The Pledge, other Courbet/Krypton/Ariane/In-Wall models) very likely each host one analogous datasheet PDF that was not individually enumerated here. The Renoir Evolution (Capsule) page had NO downloadable datasheet.

Type/format notes: 'The Wall' datasheet is served as a .jpg (image) despite the 'PDF' label. The Stellar datasheet link is a WordPress attachment page (/nouvelle-fiche-technique-stellar-fr-final_compressed/) rather than a direct file. The Courbet N8 page also links a third-party magazine review (HifiTest, German) that is re-hosted on the official domain; included as a white paper/review. The /archives/ page lists 40+ discontinued/legacy model sub-pages (Atmosphere, Balthus, Basson, Cezanne, Matisse, MIA, in-wall 130/170 RO, etc.) but those legacy pages were not individually opened; any legacy datasheets they host were not enumerated within budget, so no legacy=true documents are recorded.
